Do not go gentle into that good night,

Old age should burn and rave at close of day;

Rage, rage against the dying of the light.

I first heard this poem in Interstellar, and I thought it sounded pretty cool. I understood the basis of it, but most of it was just a bit too 'poemy' to understand. Then I decided to find out what the individual lines meant (turns out it also has 6 stanzas), and what I found was pretty kickass.

I went to this site to figure out what it meant[1] , and it turned out to be one of the most inspirational literary works I have ever read.

Apparently the author, Dylan Thomas, wrote it after he watched his father die. He was frustrated by how his father, sick, weak, and on his deathbed, just gave up and accepted death.

In the poem, Thomas passionately encourages him to fight the inevitable and muster up all the strength he has to stay alive. He also writes some powerful words addressed to different men, about how they should face death.

I interpreted this piece as being to just one person, the audience, but intended to reach out various aspects of that person.

  • The wise men, a person's intelligent side, should actually think about what's around them and express it. Whether it's injustice, scientific facts, or anything that makes an impact in the lives of others. If the words of a single person causes others to think and make a difference, then that person has lived.

  • The good men, a person's moral side, shouldn't be all talk. I'm guilty myself of having a good idea, taking pleasure in having that idea, then doing absolutely nothing with it. In old age, I don't want to look back and regret not taking education seriously, I don't want to regret not taking care of my body, and I don't want to regret not traveling the world. I want to look back at my life and be happy that I did everything that I wanted to, and not wish I had more time to do those things.

  • The wild men, a person's anxious side, should become more mindful. A common mindset is that people should make the most of their short lives on earth. However, many people take this too far and worry that they might be wasting time and end up over thinking and becoming unhappy. Stop and smell the flowers. Decisions should be evaluated, but not to the point that they overwhelm life and waste time.

  • The grave men, a person's weaknesses, shouldn't let those weaknesses define them. Sure, any weaknesses are very difficult to live with, and sure, some people have been dealt some pretty bad cards. But what will being upset do? I could list for days people that have overcome a bad situation and become successful. They didn't let weakness define them, they worked day in and day out to let their achievements define them.

Will you let death wipe you away and leave any remnants of you? Or will you take on life, fearless and determined to do everything you can to make the best of this awesome gift?

Do not go gentle into that good night.

Rage, rage against the dying of the light.
